title: Solubilization and Bio-conjugation of Quantum Dots and Bacterial Toxicity Assays by Growth Curve and Plate Count
protocol: Prepare a solution of CdTe QDs in toluene at 15 μM.
Transfer 200 μL of the CdTe QD stock into a glass vial.
Add 800 μL toluene, 1 mL of 200 mM borate buffer (pH 9), and 2 μL of 11.5 M mercaptopropionic acid (MPA).
Cap the vial and shake vigorously for 30-60 seconds.
Remove and discard the toluene layer.
Transfer the aqueous phase into a clean vial.
Purify the solubilized QDs by washing/filtering four times using a 500 μL, 10000 molecular weight cutoff centrifuge filter at 3000 x g for 13 minutes.
Suspend the washed QDs in 50 mM borate buffer at the desired pH and store at 4°C.
Dissolve polymyxin B in H2O at 60 μM.
Calculate the amount of QD solution needed for bacterial toxicity experiments.
Prepare two tubes containing 100 μL of 1 μM quantum dots in 50 mM borate buffer.
If coupling to a primary amine, prepare a 19 mg/mL (100 mM) solution of EDC in H2O.
Add 50 μL of the 10x antibiotic solution to the conjugate tube for PMB:CdTe conjugation at molar ratio of 30:1.
If needed, add 1 μL of the EDC stock solution to the conjugate tube.
Bring up the conjugate volume to 0.5 mL with borate buffer or PBS.
Shield tubes from light with aluminum foil.
Place tubes on a nutator or rocker for 1 hour.
Wash the conjugates by passing through an appropriate filter.
Estimate the number of antibiotic molecules per QD using absorbance, fluorescence spectroscopy, gel electrophoresis, or FTIR.
Seed 10 mL of bacterial growth medium from a fresh colony using sterile and biosafety technique in the evening, two days before the conjugation experiment.
Fill each well of a clear-bottom 96-well plate with nearly maximal amount of growth medium one to two hours before the experiment.
Use a multichannel pipette to seed each well with 1-50 μL of bacterial culture.
Put the plate onto the plate reader and set it to read every 10 minutes for 2 hours at a determined wavelength.
Monitor the plate so that bacteria do not grow too dense too quickly.
When cells reach OD=0.1-0.15, remove the plate from the plate reader and stop the recording.
Add drug alone and QDs alone at different concentrations in triplicates.
Use one side of the plate as a "dark" control and one half to be illuminated.
Shield the "dark" side of the plate with aluminum foil.
Expose the other side to a lamp at the desired wavelength.
Irradiate for 30-60 min using a custom 96-well, 440-nm lamp made from 2.4 mW LEDs.
Place an empty column between the exposed and unexposed sides of the plate if necessary.
Put the plate into the plate reader after light exposure.
Record OD 600 every 10 minutes for 5-12 hours depending on growth rate.
Keep the temperature below 32 °C to avoid drying of the cultures.
The day before the experiment, seed 10 mL of culture from a fresh colony into appropriate rich medium using correct sterile and biosafety technique.
Fill each well of a clear-bottom 96-well plate with nearly maximal amount of growth medium one to two hours before the experiment.
Seed each well with 1-50 μL of bacterial culture using a multichannel pipette.
Put the plate onto the plate reader.
Set the plate reader to read every 10 minutes for 2 hours at the same wavelength used in Part 3.
Remove the plate from the plate reader when cells reach an OD of 0.1-0.15.
Add QD conjugates at different concentrations in at least quadruplicate.
Use one side of the plate as a "dark" control and the other half to be illuminated.
Include a bacteria-only control strip on every plate.
Include single strips for drug only and QD only controls.
Shield the "dark" side of the plate with aluminum foil.
Expose the other side to a lamp at the desired wavelength.
Place the plate into the plate reader after light exposure.
Record OD 600 every 10 minutes for 5-12 hours.
Maintain the temperature below 32 °C to prevent drying of cultures.
Choose one or more wells of the treated 96-well plate for serial dilutions and colony counting.
Dilute each selected bacterial sample with PBS or saline solution (0.9 % NaCl).
Transfer 20 μL of the bacterial solution to 180 μL saline solution, change pipette tip, mix.
Repeat the dilution process six times.
Take 10 μL from each dilution and plate on an appropriate solid media plate.
Incubate the plated samples at the appropriate temperature for 16 hours.
Count colonies and calculate colony forming units (CFU) using the formula (# of colonies x dilution factor)/volume plated= CFU/mL.
